summary.intent: Run a wave of parallel agents (part of a larger sweep) to harden the codebase, including one agent writing pinning tests that kill surviving cargo-mutants mutants in search, token, and TypeScript extraction code without changing production behavior.
summary.outcome: The pinning-tests agent opened PR #42 (four test-only commits, suite at 743 passing, lint and typos clean), killing most mutants; five survivors remain, mostly claimed equivalent but unverified. #40 has merged, #41 and #42 are open for review, the stack-overflow fix (trail 184) is still running, and the sweep's Phase 1 is on hold awaiting the user's go.

repo: Project uses `just lint` and `just typos` as pre-PR checks; the suite is at 743 tests.
Mutation testing is done with cargo-mutants, re-run per file to verify that new tests kill targeted mutants.
Tests that need unreadable files use a non-UTF-8 line instead of chmod, so they don't depend on root or unix permissions.
macOS cannot create non-UTF-8 file names, so tests for that path are gated to non-macOS and only run on Linux CI.
The token count is capped at 32 KiB: texts under it must equal the real o200k count, and larger texts fall back to byte length.
`tokenize` already splits on every non-alphanumeric character, which makes some guards in tokens.rs and bm25.rs redundant (equivalent mutants).
Search pre-checks return all root errors before the walk starts, so the bad-root handling in the walk cannot change behavior.

code.finding: Surviving mutant on bad search root handling; claimed equivalent because pre-checks return root errors before the walk. A CLI test for a missing root was added instead.
Non-UTF-8 path counter mutant survives on macOS since such file names can't be created; an existing non-macOS-gated test should kill it on Linux CI but hasn't been run.
Surviving mutant claimed equivalent because tokenize already splits on every non-alphanumeric.
Surviving mutant claimed equivalent because the formula already returns 0.0 in those cases.

workflow: Worktree-isolated background agents each produce a PR and report via a handback message; task notifications can arrive while an agent still has background work running, so the result may be interim.
Equivalence claims for surviving mutants should be confirmed by a different reviewer agent rather than the agent that wrote the tests, as a sweep rule.
When a mutant can't be killed, pinning current behavior with an explicit test (e.g. parenthesised default export for preserve_parens) is an acceptable fallback.

friction: Five mutants survived; three are claimed equivalent and one environmental, with none independently verified.
The preserve_parens mutant had no input that differed in output, so only current behavior could be pinned.
The non-UTF-8 path test cannot run on macOS, so Linux CI is the only way to confirm it kills the mutant.
The depth scanner produced 13 timed-out mutants alongside 143 caught.
open_items: Have a different agent confirm the equivalence claims for the survivors at text_search.rs:134, tokens.rs:79 and bm25.rs:52; the assistant offered to add this to Phase 4 of the sweep.
Run the non-macOS-gated test on Linux CI to confirm it kills the non-UTF-8 path counter mutant at text_search.rs:147.
Wait for the stack-overflow fix (trail 184), the last wave-1 agent.
The sweep's Phase 1 is on hold until the user says go.
